subject: Reserve plan: throughput, GPU preference & unit-econ check
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@neotech.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Reserve plan: throughput, GPU preference & unit-econ check

Hi Daniel — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can size a dedicated lane and prepare a firm pilot quote.

Summary from the call:
- App workload: extractive Q&A + short-form summarization API called from web app and nightly batch jobs.
- Current latency target: p95 <= 400ms for interactive routes; batch can be higher.
- Example average prompt+generation length we saw: ~450 tokens input, ~150 tokens output (avg 600 tokens per call).
- Peak concurrency observed in demo: ~8-12 qps; expected steady-state after rollout: 4-6 qps.

Open asks to confirm so we can propose GPU type + reserved size and unit economics ($/1M tokens):
1) Target daily tokens (or avg qps over business hours) we should plan for (please give a low/expected/high range).
2) Monthly budget range for inference (ballpark is fine: e.g., $5k-$15k/month).
3) Preference for HW: do you have a hard requirement for H100, or is an A100/80GB acceptable if it hits latency/throughput targets?
4) Procurement timeline / PO cadence (pilot first? 30/60/90 day commitment?)

What we'll propose after your answers: a 2-week pilot configuration (reserved lane + burst), and 1) conservative reserve (single GPU lane) and 2) performance reserve (multi-GPU) with projected $/1M-token ranges and throughput estimates.

Thanks — once you confirm the three numbers above I’ll ask Laura to produce the two-option pricing sheet and a short throughput appendix.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachment: none in this message
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@neotech.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@neotech.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 23:40:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Reserve plan: throughput, GPU preference & unit-econ check

Thanks Karthik — good summary. Answers inline: 

1) Token volumes: low ~3M tokens/day, expected ~12M tokens/day, high ~25M tokens/day (spike during monthly reports).
2) Monthly inference budget: target $8k/month initially; can stretch to $15k/month if we see conversion lift.
3) HW preference: we prefer H100 for latency-sensitive routes if cost delta is reasonable, but A100 is acceptable for pilot if you can demonstrate p95 latency under 400ms for our profile.
4) Timeline: want pilot in May. Procurement usually picks up after pilot (30–60 day net).

Also: we need standard SOC2-related language in the quote for our procurement team, and a short note on how you handle KV cache/TTL (we push some prompts from the user session into cache).

-Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform, Neotech Health
daniel.park@neotech.ai | +1 (617) 555-2234

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 14:10, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Daniel — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can size a dedicated lane and prepare a firm pilot quote.
> ...
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@neotech.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 02:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Reserve plan: throughput, GPU preference & unit-econ check

Karthik / Ben — following Daniel's numbers here are two recommended reserve configurations and the unit-econ we can show in the pilot. I included the throughput appendix as an attachment.

Option A — Cost-first (fit within $8k/mo target):
- Config: 1 x A100 80GB reserved lane (with 2x burst capacity for short spikes)
- Expected steady throughput: ~6 qps at avg 600 tokens/call (estimated ~12M tokens/day steady)
- Projected unit cost: $28–$34 per 1M tokens (depends on burst usage & batching)
- Notes: Can meet ~p95 450–500ms for interactive routes; batch jobs will be cheaper.

Option B — Performance-first (preferred if H100 chosen):
- Config: 1 x H100 reserved lane or 2 x A100 equivalent (if H100 availability is constrained we recommend 2x A100)
- Expected steady throughput: ~10–12 qps at avg 600 tokens/call (covers higher spikes up to 25M tokens/day with burst policy)
- Projected unit cost: $18–$26 per 1M tokens (H100 gives better perf/price at higher throughput)
- Notes: p95 latency should be within 300–400ms interactive with KV caching enabled and continuous batching tuned.

Commitment/contract: 30-day pilot (billed pro-rata) -> typical reserved terms 3/6/12 months with volume discounts. We will include SOC2 statement language in the quote and a short section on cache TTL and request routing (to satisfy procurement).

Attachments included: throughput-estimates.pdf (per-config qps -> token/day curves), neotech-reserve-pricing-sheet.xlsx (line-item pricing and optional add-ons).

I recommend we offer Option A as the low-friction pilot and present Option B as the scalable upgrade path (with an H100 price outline). Ben — can you sign off on the $/1M ranges? If yes I’ll generate the pilot PDF quote to send to Daniel today.

Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

> On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 23:40, Daniel Park <daniel.park@neotech.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks Karthik — good summary. Answers inline: ...
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@neotech.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserve plan: throughput, GPU preference & unit-econ check

Thanks Daniel — appreciate the ranges, that’s exactly what we needed. Next steps and proposal so we’re aligned: 

1) Pilot request: we propose a 2-week pilot starting the week of May 10. Pilot config: Option A (1 x A100 80GB reserved lane) to prove latency/throughput and baseline unit-econ. If you prefer we can swap to 1 x H100 for pilot (adds delta to cost paper).
2) Deliverables during pilot: throughput dashboard (per-route), token-level cost breakdown, KV cache behavior summary, and a one-page SOC2 statement for procurement.
3) Pricing: attached is a short pilot quote (redwood-pilot-quote-neotech_v1.pdf). Pilot billing is pro-rata; pro forma pricing for after-pilot reserve shown in the attached pricing sheet.
4) Ask from Neotech: a short confirmation of preferred pilot GPU (A100 OR H100) and a PO/approval contact for procurement so we can schedule billing.

If you confirm GPU preference and procurement contact I’ll circulate the official pilot SOW and ticket it for May 10 kickoff. Ben / Laura — please confirm the pricing lines and I’ll send the quote to Daniel.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-pilot-quote-neotech_v1.pdf, neotech-reserve-pricing-sheet.xlsx
